title: Floating-point endpoint drift can delete grid-aligned boundary layers
reason: New coordinator-run source-based synthetic evidence shows that nearly constant Savitzky-Golay endpoint outputs drift across exactly aligned voxel coordinates. Hard Z>=lower and Z<=upper tests then remove whole boundary layers despite negligible physical endpoint change. This is a numerical reproducibility defect, not evidence of anatomical shape uncertainty.
criterion: Document and test a coordinate/grid-scaled numerical tolerance for interval membership, distinguish it from physical mask dilation or model error, and compare legacy and corrected reference results. Test aligned and near-boundary endpoints at multiple voxel spacings; verify tolerance does not add arbitrary layers or mask real geometric changes. Keep the legacy kernel unchanged in the archive.
evidence: Versioned reference-membership change, synthetic regression tests and both legacy/reference output tables with precise tolerance and units.
discovery: Discovered after initial round-1 report from coordinator-generated deterministic kernel ablations; this is an explicit new finding, not an unstated change to acceptance criteria.
